tasks.short: Check monitor values, blood gas and lab results against the patient, decide whether emergency action is needed, and call for it.

steps.what: Nurse validates the hourly monitor values in the patient data system and removes artefacts
Nurse opens separate screens for new laboratory and blood gas results
Nurse looks at the patient: consciousness, skin, breathing and perfusion
Nurse evaluates whether the values call for an emergency intervention under protocol
Nurse calls the intensivist and starts first actions
Intensivist assesses and orders the intervention
Nurse types the evaluation, times and actions into the record afterwards

tasks.design: Configure one bedside view in the patient data system ({OTHER}) that puts the latest blood gas, lactate, potassium and other key results next to the validated vital signs, flagging values outside the unit's protocol limits. Event buttons time-stamp calls and first actions so the note is completed, not retyped; the evaluation and the call stay with the nurse.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results and vital signs sat on different screens, and events were reconstructed after the emergency.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient data systems support combined views, limit flags and event buttons as configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a patient needs action now is clinical judgement; too many flags cause alarm fatigue.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that numbers and patient do not match and acting before the next value confirms it.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; results are in one place when deciding.

reach.task: Review results on the morning round
reach.learn: Whether the same combined view shortens the round.

evidence.claim: Patient data systems in intensive care can combine vital signs and lab results in one view with limit flags and event buttons.
AI in medical devices that need a notified body is high-risk under the AI Act, so this design keeps to fixed protocol limits.
The record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from new values to the call and first actions; treatment by the intensivist is outside.

Input contract: vital signs from monitors validated by the nurse; lab and blood gas results sent by the lab and analysers to the patient data system; limits per value set by the unit's protocol committee; fallback is the separate screens.
Monitor charting already runs; that runtime earns no saving.
Intensivist time is outside the nurse's savings.
unknowns: Whether the unit's patient data system shows lab results today.
How many emergency calls per shift.
research_questions: Do protocol flags shorten the time from abnormal value to call?

already_counted.description: Nurse acknowledges limit flags in the combined view.

incremental.description: Nurse reports flags that fire too often or too late.
Protocol committee keeps limits current and reviews flag rates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Units whose patient data system already shows results beside vitals save only on event recording.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch for deterioration such as sepsis or shock, screen at set times, alert the intensivist, start the bundle and track it.

steps.what: Nurse monitors patients for changes in status: perfusion, mental state, temperature
Nurse fills in the paper sepsis screening checklist at set times
Nurse alerts the intensivist when sepsis or shock is suspected
Intensivist assesses and orders the sepsis bundle
Nurse institutes appropriate interventions: cultures, fluids, antibiotics, vasopressors
Nurse notes bundle times on paper and copies them into the record
Nurse reassesses blood pressure, lactate and urine output after fluids

tasks.design: The paper screening checklist becomes a form in the patient data system ({OTHER}) that fills the hospital's fixed screening criteria from charted vitals and labs, leaving only the clinical items for the nurse. Once the intensivist orders the bundle, times for cultures, antibiotics and fluids are taken from orders and bedside administration scans into a bundle timer; no prediction model is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Screening and bundle times lived on paper, so compliance was measured by hand from records afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient data systems support forms that pull charted values, and bedside scanning time-stamps administrations.
tasks.still_hard: Sepsis is recognised at the bedside; even fixed score calculators can count as medical device software, so the record's own certified module or a validated protocol form is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a patient is going off before any score changes.

ambition.what: Every patient screened at every set time, with bundle times measured rather than reconstructed.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; screening and timing paperwork shrink.

reach.task: Screen deteriorating ward patients for sepsis
reach.learn: Whether the same form works where vitals are charted less often.

evidence.claim: Decision software in care is usually a medical device of class IIa or higher.
AI in medical devices that need a notified body is high-risk under the AI Act from August 2028.
Patient data systems can pre-fill screening forms from charted values and time-stamp scanned administrations.

assumptions: Boundary: from watching for deterioration to the response assessment after the bundle; further treatment is outside.

Input contract: vitals validated by nurses in the patient data system; lab results from the lab; screening criteria set by the hospital's sepsis working group; administrations scanned at the bedside by nurses; fallback is the paper checklist.
Intensivist time is outside the nurse's savings.
Bedside watching and interventions do not change.
unknowns: Whether the unit screens on paper or in the record today.
Share of administrations scanned at the bedside.
research_questions: Does the bundle timer change time to antibiotics?

already_counted.description: Nurse checks the pre-filled screen and completes the clinical items.

incremental.description: Nurse corrects missed scans so bundle times are right.
Sepsis working group keeps criteria current and reviews bundle compliance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Units with few sepsis cases or low bedside scanning keep most paper timing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record fluid intake and output hourly, total the balance, compare with electrolytes and weight, and act on imbalances.

steps.what: Nurse reads infusion pump volumes and enters hourly fluid intake
Nurse empties and reads urine meters and drains and notes output
Nurse adds up intake and output on the paper fluid chart each shift
Nurse compares the balance with electrolytes, weight and creatinine
Nurse judges emerging fluid and electrolyte imbalances and acts under protocol
Cardiologist adjusts fluid, diuretic or electrolyte orders

tasks.design: Infusion pumps send delivered volumes to the fluid balance in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) once each pump is paired to the patient by scan; the nurse adds oral intake and readings of urine meters and drains. Hourly, shift and cumulative balance are computed and shown beside electrolytes, weight and creatinine, and the judgement and action stay with the nurse and cardiologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pumps were not linked to the record, so volumes were read off displays and totalled on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Pump integration with hospital records exists, and records compute fluid balances as configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Pump pairing must be right every time; urine and drain readings stay manual.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a positive balance and a rising weight mean the heart is not coping, and acting early.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; adding up disappears and the balance is always current.

reach.task: Track fluid removal and weight between sessions
reach.learn: Whether pump-fed balances suit dialysis records.

evidence.claim: Infusion pumps can send delivered volumes to hospital records after pairing with the patient.
The inspectorate names errors from wrong registration as a risk providers must manage.
The record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Scenario: a coronary care unit on the general hospital record with paper fluid charts; units with a patient data system that already computes balances save less.
Input contract: pump volumes with patient pairing scanned by the nurse at connection; oral intake and output entered by nurses; lab results from the lab; fallback is the paper chart.
Boundary: from hourly recording to the action on imbalance; prescribing is outside.
Cardiologist time is outside the nurse's savings.
unknowns: Whether the unit's pump model supports integration.
How fluid balances are kept today.
research_questions: Do computed balances catch fluid overload earlier than paper totals?

already_counted.description: Nurse validates imported pump volumes each hour.

incremental.description: Medical technology keeps the pump integration working.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If pump integration fails often, nurses go back to reading displays and typing intake.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take handover, build the shift worklist, assess each patient, prioritise care and re-plan when a patient deteriorates.

steps.what: Nurse receives the bedside handover for assigned patients
Nurse copies due medication, turns, lab draws and dressings from several screens onto a paper worklist
Nurse assesses each critically ill patient at the start of the shift
Nurse sets priorities across assigned patients and plans the shift
Nurse re-plans when a patient deteriorates or an admission arrives
Charge nurse redistributes patients when workload changes
Nurse ticks off done tasks on paper and later again in the record

tasks.design: The electronic health record ({OTHER}) generates a per-patient shift worklist from active orders, the medication schedule and care plan actions, sorted by due time, for the nurse to check at the start of the shift. Tasks are ticked off once on the worklist and written to the record; prioritising and re-planning stay with the nurse.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due tasks were spread over medication, order and care plan screens, so nurses copied them by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Records can list due items across orders and care plans as a configured worklist.
tasks.still_hard: Priorities change by the minute with the patient's condition; tasks agreed verbally are not in the record.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what matters most for a critically ill patient right now and changing course without losing the thread.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the start of the shift goes to patients instead of copying.

reach.task: Plan routine care tasks for the shift
reach.learn: Whether a shared worklist helps nurse and assistant split tasks.

evidence.claim: Hospital records can generate due-task worklists from orders, medication schedules and care plans.
The record is kept twenty years after the last change.
Providers are responsible for careful introduction and testing of new software in care.

assumptions: Boundary: one shift from handover to tasks completed; care itself is outside.
Input contract: active orders entered by physicians, medication schedule from the pharmacy check, care plan actions entered by nurses; fallback is the paper worklist.
Charge nurse time is outside the nurse's savings.
Handover, assessment and prioritising do not change.
unknowns: How the unit builds worklists today.
research_questions: Do generated worklists reduce missed due tasks?

already_counted.description: Nurse checks the generated worklist for missing or wrong items.

incremental.description: Nurse adds verbally agreed tasks to the worklist.
Application manager keeps worklist rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Units where most tasks are agreed at the bedside and not ordered in the record gain little from the worklist.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The critical care nurse keeps watching, judging and acting; reading screens, totalling charts and copying worklists shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A critical care nurse whose charts, balances and worklists are always current, so attention stays on the patient.
